newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Riksbank cuts rate corridor, repo rate.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Riksbank cuts rate corridor, repo rate.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank (central bank) cut on Thursday its interest rate corridor by 50 basis points and announced a 25 basis point cut in its key repo rate to take effect on Tuesday.
The new repo rate of 4.60 percent will apply for the next three weekly repo tenders, the Riksbank said in a statement.

"Today, the Governing Board of the Riksbank has decided to lower both the deposit and the lending rate by 0.5 percentage points," the Riksbank said in a statement, adding that the decision would be effective as of October 30, 1996.
The deposit rate is now set at 4.25 percent and the lending rate at 5.75 percent.
In a surprise move, the Riksbank also said governor Urban Backstrom had decided to lower the repo rate at Tuesday's auction by 0.25 percentage points to 4.60 percent.
This rate will also apply for the following three repo tenders on November 5, 12 and 19, the Riksbank said.
"The decisions are based on the assessment that the outlook for inflation in the coming years remains in line with the inflation target.
"The future monetary stance will depend on new information and how it relates to the analysis in the Riksbank's laterst (September) inflation report," the bank said.
It said it would hold a news conference at 1000 GMT on Thursday.
